lesson_title: Card, String and a Cotton Reel
hook_text: Three sheets of card, four skewers, a cotton reel and some string. By the end of the period it lifts steel out of a pile and drops it in a bin.
clip_script: Follow the chart. Base first: double card, cut on the mat, glued, pressed under a book. Mast: roll the card tight round a pencil until it is a tube that will not bend. Arm: another tube, stiff before light. While the glue dries, the winch: cotton reel on a skewer, handle out at right angles, cheeks either side, a bead so it spins, a peg so it cannot run back. Pulley: a bead through the arm's tip with cheeks. Now assemble. Mast on the cross with gussets. Arm on the mast with a sleeve. Winch right under the mast so the string runs straight. Up, along, over, magnet on. Cells at the back, wired like the diagram. Press. Light on. Lower, lift to 150, swing 200, let go. Steel in the bin, foil left behind, base still down. Three times, all written down.
visual_style: Whiteboard base, tube, arm appearing; a cotton reel with handle and cheeks; parts sliding together; a string path highlighted up and over; clips crossing to a bin.
mood: Busy and triumphant, a build coming together.
pacing: Base, mast, arm, winch, pulley, assemble, string, test, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build your crane from your own drawing.
